version.approval_notes: Kits Editor for Firefox restyles Firefox's own interface (tab bar, toolbar, address bar), which extensions can't do directly, so it uses userChrome.css. A separate native messaging helper (native-host/ in the source repo; Python standard library only) is installed by the user with native-host/install.sh or install.ps1. When the user presses Apply on the settings page, the helper writes the generated stylesheet to <profile>/chrome/ and an allowlisted set of prefs to user.js; the settings page lists those prefs before Apply. Any rules already in userChrome.css are moved to userChrome.css.ahtb-backup (they would override the generated stylesheet), as the settings page says before Apply; Remove from Firefox puts them back. The prefs are dropped from user.js once Firefox has saved them, so they apply once. To test: 1) install the helper: curl -fsSL https://github.com/mattsaund/kits-firefox-plugin/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh  2) open the extension's settings page (toolbar button), choose a layout, press Apply  3) restart Firefox. The optional technicalAndInteraction data permission gates a twice-daily request to api.github.com for the latest release; no user data is sent and the add-on works fully without it. The optional <all_urls> host permission is requested only when the user switches on "Let clicks through to the page" on the settings page. It registers content/click-through.js, which checks whether the element under the pointer near a window edge is clickable and tells the background script on/off; the background script shows or hides the add-on's page action on that tab, which the generated stylesheet reads as a per-tab flag (the stylesheet hides the page action icon). No page content is stored or sent anywhere. Switching it off removes the permission and the content script. While that option is on, the background script also runs an empty function in the active tab with scripting.executeScript; if Firefox refuses (another extension's page, about: pages), the page action is shown with a different title, which the stylesheet reads as 'hover zones no deeper than 10px on this tab'. The optional "management" permission is requested only when the user switches on "Show my themes" on the settings page. It is used to list installed themes (management.getAll, filtered to type "theme") and to switch theme (management.setEnabled on a theme), including when the user loads a saved profile that records a theme. Other add-ons are not listed, changed or reported anywhere. Saved profiles stay in storage.local. Full source: https://github.com/mattsaund/kits-firefox-plugin
